data.name: Esharvansh
data.gender_notes: Esharvansh is used as a male name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Derived from 'Esh' (Lord) and 'Arvansh' (Descendants of Gods). Refers to one who is the descendant of the gods. The name Esharvansh carries the meaning “Lord of Gods” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Sanskrit tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit, Marathi. Parents who choose Esharvansh usually hope their child will grow to embody lord of gods and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.etymology: Esharvansh belongs to the Sanskrit linguistic tradition and is used in Hindu naming. Its recorded meaning is “Lord of Gods.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Esharvansh total 7, giving a life-path number of 7. Number 7 is linked with Ketu and with the qualities of reflection, wisdom and inner depth.

data.cultural_impact: The name Esharvansh carries a rich cultural heritage as it is derived from ancient Hindu scriptures and signifies being a descendant of the gods. In Hindu society, this name bears an immense sense of pride and honor as it indicates a deep connection to the divine and the Hindu gods. It also represents a deep-rooted spiritual belief and a strong sense of heritage that holds significance in the Indian subcontinent.
data.spiritual_significance: The spiritual significance of the name Esharvansh is rooted in the Hindu belief that every human being is a descendant of the gods and carries the divine energy within them. This name serves as a constant reminder of our spiritual connection to the divine and the importance of living a spiritual life. It is a source of motivation and inspiration for individuals to strive towards elevating their spiritual consciousness and reaching divine levels of consciousness.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Esharvansh signifies the illustrious lineage of the divine sage Eshar, symbolizing wisdom, knowledge, and enlightenment passed down through generations. It is a reminder of one's connection to the divine and the pursuit of spiritual growth.

historical_references.reference: The Esharvansh was a royal dynasty in ancient India, originating from the Solar Dynasty (Suryavansha) of the Lunar Dynasty (Chandravansha). The name 'Eshar' is derived from the Vedic deity Ashrava, who was believed to be the god of prosperity and fertility. The Esharvansh ruled over the kingdom of Haihayas in the northern part of India, particularly around the present-day region of Uttar Pradesh.

Another reference to the Esharvansh comes from the Mahabharata, an ancient Indian epic. In this text, the Esharvansh is mentioned as the dynasty of King Ikshvaku, the progenitor of the Solar Dynasty (Suryavansha). The Esharvansh is described as the lineage of kings who ruled over the regions of Kosala, Magadha, and Anga, and who traced their descent from the deity Rishi Agastya.

modern_usage.modern_context: The name 'Esharvansh' is derived from ancient Hindu mythology and translates to 'the lineage of the god Eshar'. This concept of hereditary lineage is deeply rooted in Hindu culture and is often seen in various art forms, literature, and social media contexts. In literature, 'Esharvansh' can refer to the noble lineage of a character in Hindu epics, such as the Mahabharata or the Ramayana. In art and design, it can be represented through intricate depictions of Hindu gods and their lineages in temple carvings, traditional paintings, and contemporary artwork. Social media platforms, such as Instagram and Facebook, have seen an increase in the use of 'Esharvansh' as a hashtag to represent pride in one's heritage and lineage, as well as to connect with and celebrate the richness and diversity of Indian culture.
